about: Security findings of civic.promptugal.news, published at Dinis's word (18 Nov 2026, about 15:15 UTC; PrompTugal__News__Website board/guidance/2026-11-18-security-findings-published.md). A fixed finding is published in full; an open one as its title, severity and state only until it is fixed. Kept by civic.b@PrompTugal.dinis. Central log: https://promptugal.news/security/

findings.title: Any URL scheme in a markdown link in data became a link (possible stored XSS through data text)
findings.found_by: civic.b@PrompTugal.dinis, a check prompted by events.b@'s HIGH XSS finding (relayed by conductor.b@)
findings.detail: Text from data files (IMPIC's free-text contract objects, council pages) went through a step that turned [text](url) into <a href=url> for any URL. A contract object containing [x](javascript:...) would have become a clickable script link. The text itself was HTML-escaped, so no tag injection; no such text was found in the data.
findings.fix: Links only for https?://, /path or #anchor; anything else stays text. Tested with javascript:, data: and //host; every scheme-bearing href in the built site is https:.

findings.title: Reading-log page paths became links without a scheme check (self-XSS through a restored file)
findings.detail: The account page and the reading graph turned each page path in the browser's reading log into a link. 'Restore from a file' lets a reader load a log from a file, so a crafted file could put a javascript: path there and run when the reader clicked it in their own browser.
findings.fix: Paths pass safeHref (site-relative or http(s) only, else #) before becoming links.

findings.title: Live contracts script: hardening points found in the security post-review, before release
findings.found_by: civic.b.security@PrompTugal.dinis (Sonnet), security post-review of the diff before commit
findings.detail: No high or medium issue. Low: contract text withheld only on the feed's own flag (a feed error could show text beside 'a private individual'); body size checked only after reading; redirects followed; control and bidi characters not stripped; the gate's host check could be fooled by user info in a URL.
findings.fix: Privacy decided in the page (text withheld unless every supplier is a company with a company NIF); body read as a stream and stopped at 5 MB; redirects refused; control and bidi characters stripped; the gate's host check tightened and a missing script caught. Tested with a hostile feed (HTML, javascript: links, bad price and date, a natural person, __proto__) and a failing feed.

findings.title: Supplier names could read as markdown (links or bold) on pages; AI list relied on the data to withhold private contracts
findings.file: scripts/generate.mjs (supplier names in tables and company pages; the tech and AI page)
findings.found_by: civic.b.security@PrompTugal.dinis (Sonnet), security post-review of the tech and AI page before commit
findings.detail: Names are HTML-escaped, but a name containing [text](https://...) would have shown as a link, and asterisks as bold (33 names in 2025 and 2026 contain such characters). The AI list relied on the extracted data having no text for contracts with a private individual, which held for all 848 such contracts but was not checked in the page code.
findings.fix: Supplier names shown with [ ] as ( ) and * as a middle dot; the AI list skips any contract with a withheld supplier, whatever the data says.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy on any page
findings.found_by: civic.b@PrompTugal.dinis (backlog); design pre-reviewed and diff post-reviewed by civic.b.security@PrompTugal.dinis (Sonnet)
findings.detail: Without a policy, any script that reached a page (through a future raw HTML block or a compromised data value) could run and send data anywhere. None is known to have done so.
findings.fix: A meta Content-Security-Policy on every page, kept once in scripts/csp.mjs: scripts only from this site, connections only to the five hosts the pages use, no objects, workers or foreign forms. The gate fails a page without exactly that policy, with an inline script or a script outside /assets/, or with an event-handler attribute (tags read quote-aware). tools/check-csp-hosts.mjs checks that the observability geo list, read at run time from promptugal.news, stays within the policy.

findings.title: No protection against being framed by another site (clickjacking)
findings.detail: frame-ancestors only works as an HTTP header, and GitHub Pages sets none. The pages have no forms or actions a framed page could be tricked into, so the risk is low. The style-src policy also allows inline styles (a stated trade: scripts stay locked).
findings.fix: Accepted for now. Needs a host that sets headers, or a header-setting proxy in front of the site.
